summary: Jitsuzo Kuwabara (1871–1931) worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1896), he held posts at Third Higher School, Tokyo Higher Normal School, and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota (born 1932) is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada from around 1962 to 1989 and succeeded Koun Yamada.

Jivnesh Sandhan specializes in computational linguistics and Indology. He earned a PhD at IIT Kanpur under Laxmidhar Behera, completed a postdoc at Kyoto University, and held posts at UC Berkeley, IIT Kanpur, and IIT Dharwad (attested 2025).

Jiyu Ren (1916–2009) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He, later teaching there (1942–1964) before directing the CASS Institute of World Religions and the National Library of China.

Jiyu-Kennett (1924–1996) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Durham University, Trinity Laban, and Sōji-ji under Keidō Chisan Kōho. She served as head priest at Unpukuji before founding Shasta Abbey in 1969, serving as abbess until 1996.
Joachim Friedrich Sprockhoff is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He completed his studies under Friedrich Otto Schrader and Helmuth von Glasenapp (until 1960).

Joachim Gentz works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He was a Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and later held posts at the University of Edinburgh as Reader in Chinese Studies and Professor.

Joachim Heidrich (1930–2004) specialized in Indology and history. He earned his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (1948–1958) under Walter Ruben and later held posts at the Zentralinstitut für Geschichte (1981–1989) and Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient (~1992–1995).

Joachim Menant (1820–1899) was an archaeologist and linguist who studied at the University of Caen Normandy. He held a post at the University of Paris and became a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1888.
Joachim Prandstetter specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his Magister degree at the University of Vienna in 1994, studying under Gerhard Oberhammer.

Joachim Wach (1898–1955) worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Leipzig, Heidelberg, Munich, Berlin, and Freiburg, he held posts at Leipzig (1924–1935), Brown University (1935–1946), and as Professor at the University of Chicago (1945–1955).

Joan Jiko Halifax (born 1942) works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Newcomb College and Union Institute & University, she held posts at Columbia, Miami, and Harvard, and founded the Ojai Foundation and Upaya Zen Center.

Joan Mascaró (1897–1987) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge from around 1926 to 1929 and served as Professor of English at the University of Barcelona in 1933.

Joanna Bialek is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who completed her PhD at the University of Marburg in 2016. She held research posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (2017–2022), Trinity College Dublin (2024–2026), and the University of Munich (2026).
Joanna Cook is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied under advisor James Laidlaw and held a post at Christ's College, Cambridge.

Joanna Gottfried Williams (1939–2022) specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University, and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1971 to 2005.

Joanna Grela is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at INALCO, Jagiellonian University (PhD, 2004), and SWPS University (habilitation, 2016), and has held a professorial post at Jagiellonian University since 2006.
Joanna Macy (1929–2025) was a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She completed her studies at Wellesley College (~1946–1950) and Syracuse University (~1973–1978).

Joanne Punzo Waghorne works in religious studies and Indology. After studying at the University of Chicago (~1971–1976), she held posts at UMass Boston, Bowdoin College, UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

Joannes van der Vliet (1847–1902) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern, later teaching Sanskrit at the University of Amsterdam and Latin at Utrecht University (1891–1892).
